$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( 1 \right).

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{{e}^{-x}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-2}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.8647\end{aligned}

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](images/72/721ca1810b816431f99bb8294f4ad12ff125342640a925035487c8ecace4eff6.svg)Therefore, we can calculate $P\left(X \geq 3\right)$ as follows:

$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161933 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-840fc6bd-43f7-5e1f-9678-e0daa00596e7" "question-b6017236-d9af-57fe-9a24-c8e569cb2642"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161748 :question/problem "Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(4\right),$ calculate $P\left(X \leq 7 \, \bigg |\, X > 5\right).$" :question/worked-solution "Given a random variable $X \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)$ and two positive real numbers $s, t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t \, \big |\, X>s) = P(X > t) = e^{-\lambda t}.
$$

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows:

$$
P(X\leq s+t \, \big|\, X>s) = 1-P(X>s+t \, \big |\, X>s) = 1-e^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda = 4,$ $s=5,$ and $s+t=7.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t = (t+s) - s =7 - 5 = 2
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 7\,|\,X>5) & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(4)\cdot (2)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-8} \\  & ≈0.999\,664.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162685 :question/problem "Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(2),$ calculate $P(X<\frac{1}{6}).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places." :question/worked-solution "An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

![](images/2a/2ae9fdb32ab1b90d11729ead5966100d53b722ce182eacfb58ff9dc7d037993f.svg)

The **rate parameter** $\lambda$ is a positive real number, and $e\approx 2.71828$ is Euler's number. 

If a random variable $X$ follows an exponential distribution, we write

$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp}(\lambda).
$$

The exponential distribution models the amount of continuous space or time between two events. In a future lesson, we will learn how to model situations using the exponential distribution. But for now, let's get some practice working with the PDF to compute probabilities." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163183 :tutorial/content "Consider a random variable $X \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda),$ and two positive real numbers $s, t.$ 

Suppose we're given that  $X>s,$ and we want to determine the probability that $X>s+t.$ In other words, we wish to compute the conditional probability 

$$
P(X>s+t \,\big|\, X>s).
$$

 

By the definition of conditional probability, we have that

$$
P(X>s+t \, \big|\, X>s) = \dfrac{P\big((X> s+t) \cap (X > s)\big)}{P(X>s)}.
$$

Notice that $X>s+t$ implies that $X>s,$ therefore

$$
P\big((X> s+t) \cap (X > s)\big) = P(X > s+t).
$$

So, the above conditional probability simplifies to

$$
P(X>s+t \,\big|\, X>s) = \dfrac{P(X> s+t )}{P(X>s)}.
$$

Next, let's recall how to calculate $P(X > a)$ for some $a>0{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>a) & =1-P(X<a) \\  & =1-{\int }_{0}^{a}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =1+{{e}^{-\lambda x}|}_{0}^{a} \\  & =1+{e}^{-\lambda a}-{e}^{0} \\  & ={e}^{-\lambda a}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can use this fact to calculate $P(X> s+t )$ and $P(X>s)$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s) & =\frac{P(X>s+t)}{P(X>s)} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-\lambda (s+t)}}{{e}^{-\lambda s}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-\lambda s}\cdot {e}^{-\lambda t}}{{e}^{-\lambda s}} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{e}^{-\lambda s}}\cdot {e}^{-\lambda t}}{\cancel{{e}^{-\lambda s}}} \\  & ={e}^{-\lambda t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, notice that $e^{-\lambda t} = P(X > t).$ So, we have proved the following property:

$$
P(X>s+t \big| X>s) = P(X > t).
$$

This property is called **memoryless property.** It can be proved that the exponential distribution is the only continuous distribution with this property (note that the geometric distribution is the only *discrete* distribution with the memoryless property).

Intuitively, the memoryless property states that the probability of an event occurring after a certain amount of time has already elapsed is independent of how much time has passed. This means that the distribution "forgets" what has happened before time $s.$ 

We'll discuss how the memoryless property is used for mathematical modeling in future lessons." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163185 :tutorial/content "Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}(2),$ let's calculate the following probability:

$$
P\left(X > \dfrac32 \,\bigg|\, X > \dfrac12\right)
$$

Given a random variable $X \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)$ and two positive real numbers $s, t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t \, \big|\, X>s) = P(X > t) = e^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
\lambda = 2, \qquad s=\dfrac 12,\qquad s+t=\dfrac32.
$$

From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t = (t+s) - s = \dfrac32-\dfrac12 = 1
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>\frac{3}{2}\,|\,X>\frac{1}{2}) & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(2)\cdot (1)} \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2}} \\  & ≈0.135\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162203 :activity/expected-seconds 840.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$

Notice that $X>s+t$ implies that $X>s,$ therefore

$$

$$

$$

$$

[{:db/id 17592186162757 :step/content {:db/id 17592186163182 :tutorial/content "A continuous random variable $X$ follows an **exponential distribution** if it has the following probability density By the definition of conditional probability, we have that

$$
P(X>s+t \, \big \mid \, X>s) = \dfrac{P\big((X> s+t) \cap (X > s)\big)}{P(X>s)}
$$

Notice that $X>s+t$ implies that $X>s$, therefore

$$
P\big((X> s+t) \cap (X > s)\big) = P(X > s+t)
$$

So, the above conditional probability simplifies to

$$
P(X>s+t \,\big \mid \, X>s) = \dfrac{P(X> s+t)}{P(X>s)}

Next, let's recall how to calculate $P(X > a)$ for some $a>0{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(X > a) &= 1 - P(X < a) \\
&= 1 - \int_{0}^{a}λe^{- λx}dx \\
&= 1 + \left.e^{- λx}\right|_{0}^{a} \\
&= 1 + e^{- λa} - e^{0} \\
&= e^{- λa}
\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}

&= \frac{e^{- λs} \cdot e^{- λt}}{e^{- λs}} \\
&= e^{- λt}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
P(X>s+t \big \mid X>s) = P(X > t)
$$
